input.candidate_text:
Take \(c=\frac27\) and \(d=5\).

For the lower bound, suppose first that \(n\ge3\). The sheet contains \(n(n-2)\) horizontal triples and \(n(n-2)\) vertical triples, for a total of \(2n(n-2)\) potential blocks. In any terminal configuration, every such triple contains a removed stamp.

A removed horizontal block meets at most five horizontal triples, since the starting position of an intersecting horizontal triple has at most five possibilities. Each of its three stamps belongs to at most three vertical triples, so the block meets at most nine vertical triples. Thus each removed block meets at most \(14\) potential triples; the same argument applies to a vertical block.

Consequently, if \(m\) blocks have been removed in a terminal configuration, then
\[
14m\ge 2n(n-2),
\]
and hence
\[
m\ge \frac17n^2-\frac27n.
\]
In particular,
\[
b(n)\ge \frac17n^2-\frac27n.
\]
For \(n=1,2\), no block can be removed, so \(b(n)=0\), and the same inequality holds.

For the upper bound, first consider the infinite integer grid. In row \(r\), designate the pairwise disjoint horizontal blocks
\[
(r,r+5k),\ (r,r+5k+1),\ (r,r+5k+2),\qquad k\in\mathbb Z.
\]
Thus the cell \((r,j)\) is designated exactly when
\[
j-r\pmod 5\in\{0,1,2\}.
\]
The only undesignated residues are \(3,4\), so every three consecutive cells in a row include a designated cell. In a fixed column, as \(r\) increases, \(j-r\pmod5\) runs through consecutive residues in reverse order. Therefore every three consecutive cells in a column also include a designated cell.

Now retain and remove only those designated horizontal blocks lying completely inside the \(n\times n\) sheet. In each row, their number is at most
\[
\left\lceil\frac{n-2}{5}\right\rceil\le \frac n5+1,
\]
so at most \(n^2/5+n\) blocks are initially removed.

If a designated cell lies inside the sheet but its designated block was not retained, then that block crosses the left or right boundary. Hence the cell lies in one of the first two or last two columns. Let \(S\) be the cells in these boundary columns; then \(|S|\le4n\).

Every triple surviving the initial removals contains a designated cell, and that cell cannot belong to a retained block. Thus every surviving triple meets \(S\). Continue greedily removing any surviving triple until none remains. Every additionally removed block contains a cell of \(S\), and these added blocks are pairwise disjoint. Therefore at most \(|S|\le4n\) additional blocks are removed.

This produces a terminal configuration using at most
\[
\frac15n^2+n+4n=\frac15n^2+5n
\]
blocks. Hence, for every positive integer \(n\),
\[
\frac17n^2-\frac27n\le b(n)\le\frac15n^2+5n.
\]
Thus the required real constants may be chosen as \(c=\frac27\) and \(d=5\).
input.theorem:
I have an \(n \times n\) sheet of stamps, from which I've been asked to tear out blocks of three adjacent stamps in a single row or column. (I can only tear along the perforations separating adjacent stamps, and each block must come out of the sheet in one piece.) Let \(b(n)\) be the smallest number of blocks I can tear out and make it impossible to tear out any more blocks. Prove that there are real constants \(c\) and \(d\) such that

\[
\frac{1}{7} n^{2}-c n \leq b(n) \leq \frac{1}{5} n^{2}+d n
\]

for all \(n>0\).
